notes:
Background: Neonforge is a mid‑market SaaS company building ProductCloud (customer-facing product search + support assistant). Started with Redwood Hosted API for rapid launch POC; now moving toward Dedicated for predictable latency/cost and VPC isolation.

POC summary: integrated hosted chat + embeddings. SE benchrun (Diego) shows 95th latency ~280ms on target model at observed QPS; thread-level recall on embeddings improved ~18% over current vector DB pipeline. POC window: 6 weeks (Jan–Feb 2026). Neonforge satisfied with output quality and reliability in test traffic.

Traffic & targets: target steady-state ~400M tokens/month in Q3, peak day spikes up to 2x baseline during marketing/product launches, concurrency target ~50 concurrent chat sessions, target p95 latency <300ms for interactive flows. Cost sensitivity: moderate — willing to commit for discount but procurement needs clear overage caps.

Dedicated pricing negotiations (current): Redwood proposed 3 commit tiers (200M / 400M / 800M tokens monthly) with stepped discounts off hosted list (approx 25% / 30% / 38%). Neonforge asks: 1) 40% discount at 400M, 2) included burst allowance (2x baseline for up to 50 hours/month) at no surcharge for first 6 months, 3) capped overage at 1.25x list rate. Finance pushing for annualized ARR predictability; prefer quarterly ramp with crediting for unused committed tokens.

Ramp & contract preferences: Neonforge prefers 6‑month ramp schedule to reach committed level: month1 = 25%, month2 = 50%, month3 = 75%, month4+ = 100% (with optional step-up option at month6). Also exploring a 12‑month commit with a 90‑day exit clause tied to SLA KPIs.

Security & compliance: require VPC private deployment for production traffic, SOC2 attestation (present), SSO via SAML, KMS key control for customer data, audit logs retention 13 months, and data residency for EU customers (must be able to route EU traffic to EU Dedicated pool). Legal flagged security appendix and data residency language as blockers.

Direct quotes / call notes: "We need to avoid surprise billing — burst has to be predictable or included" — CTO (R. Singh). "Quality delta vs current vector approach is material; cost math needs to work at scale" — Head of Product.

Communications & artifacts: Fireflies recordings attached for pricing call (FF_20260308_pricing_call). Drive deck contains Redwood proposal (linked). Two open Jira tickets for technical clarifications (INF-4821: VPC peering checklist; INF-5033: model quantization guidance).

Next steps: Redwood to produce a formal term sheet with three committed options including explicit burst allowance and overage cap. Neonforge legal to return redlines by 2026-03-24. SE to schedule final performance validation run on Dedicated staging (Diego -> week of 2026-03-15). Procurement to confirm forecast; finance to provide final ARR target for discount band.
